messages:
Aisha (docs): FYI I'm doing a quick audit of the Optimize toolkit docs — found a few broken links, and the SDK snippets for batching/caching/quant profiles are inconsistent across Python/TS. I opened a tiny PR to start fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234 :memo:
Marcus (eng-ml): Thanks — can you list the bad links? I hit one where the quant profile names don't match the runtime param names (q4_0 vs q4f).
Aisha (docs): Sure, current list: /optimize/batching -> 404, /optimize/quant-profiles -> outdated table, and examples/python/snippets.md has an old client constructor. I'll paste details in the PR comments.
Priya (devex): Quick note: the Node snippet also uses the legacy streaming API. We should unify on the new SDK snippet patterns and show both sync and streaming examples.
Sam (engineer): I can send a short Python example for the recommended batching + cache pattern. Minimal, copy/paste-ready.
Sam (engineer): ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
# prefer short timeouts for interactive routes
resp = client.generate('summarize: Keep bullets', model='redwood-2b', max_tokens=120, batch_policy='adaptive', cache_prefix_enabled=True)
print(resp.text)
```
Aisha (docs): love it. Can you add a one-liner explaining batch_policy options: 'none', 'fixed-N', 'adaptive' and default behavior?
Sam (engineer): Will do. Also adding an example config for quant profiles to avoid name mismatch:
```yaml
# recommended quant profile mapping (docs canonical)
quant_profiles:
  - name: q4_0
    runtime_aliases: [q4f, q4_0]
    description: "4-bit profile w/ fast kernels, good latency for short sequences"
  - name: q8_1
    runtime_aliases: [q8_1]
    description: "8-bit profile for heavy-throughput workloads"
```
Marcus (eng-ml): Nice. Please also add a short migration note: if you previously used 'q4f' in runtime config, map to 'q4_0' in the new toolkit examples. Saves a bunch of support tickets.
docs-bot: PR 1234 opened by @aisha/docs: "optimize: examples & link audit — batching/cache/quant" — CI: docs-lint passed :white_check_mark:
Priya (devex): For the Node/TS snippet, prefer using the new streaming pattern we shipped last month. Example: ```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
for await (const chunk of client.stream.generate({ model: 'redwood-2b', input: 'Short summary please' })) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
}
```
Aisha (docs): Good — I'll update the PR with both code blocks and add a tiny table mapping legacy param names -> canonical docs names. Also adding a 'what changed' blurb at top of page for the migration guide.
Marcus (eng-ml): Can someone volunteer to review the quant description? I want to ensure we don't accidentally claim higher accuracy for a profile that just optimizes memory.
Sam (engineer): I'll review that section tomorrow.
Priya (devex): I'll do a quick pass on the snippets for copy clarity and add inline callouts about when to prefer cache_prefix_enabled vs full KV cache.
Aisha (docs): Awesome — @Sam: update PR with Python snippet + YAML mapping. @Priya: Node snippet + copy edits. @Marcus: technical sign-off on quant text. I'll merge once the three approvals are in. ETA EOD tomorrow?
Marcus (eng-ml): EOD sounds fine.
Sam (engineer): On it.
Aisha (docs): Thanks team! I'll drop a short changelog entry and a link to the internal migration checklist after merge. :rocket:
